thread.title: Stock Market Today: Boeing, IBM Drag On Dow | Investor's Business Daily

author: NANCY GONDO
title: Stock Market Today: Boeing, IBM Drag On Dow | Investor's Business Daily
text:
The stock market today moved sharply in the red after the major market indexes gave up big early gains. President Trump's threat to slap tariffs on all Chinese goods contributed to the reversal, though he has made that threat before.
X Weaker-than-expected U.S. economic data didn't help. Personal income for September climbed 0.2% month over month, missing views for 0.4%. The Dallas Federal Reserve's manufacturing survey for October came in at 17.6, vs. the previous reading of 23.3.
Tech stocks were the culprit again in the stock market today , as they have been recently. The Nasdaq composite shed 2%, the Dow Jones industrial Average slipped nearly 1.3% and the S&P 500 gave up 1%. Small caps outperformed, however, as the Russell 2000 advanced 0.3%.
Volume was tracking lower on the NYSE and Nasdaq vs. the same time Friday, potentially easing the sting of the reversals.
Boeing ( BA ) led the Dow losers with a 7% drop, falling well below its 200-day moving average for the first time in two years. Shares dived following news of a crash of one of its 737 Max airplanes.
Stock Market Today: These Techs Drag On Dow Big-cap techs also weighed on the blue-chip index. IBM ( IBM ), Microsoft ( MSFT ) and Apple ( AAPL ) lost 3%, 2% and 1%, respectively. IBM announced that it will buy open-source systems provider Red Hat ( RHT ) for $34 billion . IBM initially slumped 5% before paring some of its losses. Red Hat soared 45%.
Apple continues to consolidate just below its 50-day line and may be forming a new base with a 233.57 potential buy point . Two possible catalysts this week: a product launch event Tuesday and quarterly earnings on Thursday after the close. Analysts expect the iPhone maker to earn $2.78 a share on $61.59 billion in revenue, which would mark respective increases of 34% and 17%.
In the IBD 50 , Roper Technologies ( ROP ), Viper Energy Partners ( VNOM ) and Cactus ( WHD ) led the downside with losses of more than 2.5% each.
But discount retailers were a bright spot as Dollar General ( DG ), TJX ( TJX ) and Five Below ( FIVE ) each gained 1% to 2% or more. The top-ranked Retail-Discount & Variety group advanced 2%, while TJX's Retail-Apparel/Shoes/Accessories group rose 2.5%.
The Innovator IBD 50 ETF ( FFTY ), up in the early going, fell nearly 0.9%.
